A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Reflective Memory Management (RMM) work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching analyses moved from appendices into the main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original MSC and LongMemEval experiments, component ablations, retrieval analyses, citation-score validation and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a human evaluation measuring agreement with the MSC LLM judge.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, memory extraction and merging, reranker architecture, Gumbel sampling, citation rewards and REINFORCE updates are unchanged. Section 5 clarifies the meaning of a topic without changing the procedure or prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate personalized response generation on MSC and long-term conversational question answering on LongMemEval. The added human evaluation samples existing MSC instances without introducing another domain, population or task scenario.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain No History, Long Context, RAG, MemoryBank and LD-Agent, including the same retriever, generator and oracle variants. Newly cited memory systems do not enter the reported benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 8.8 adds an evaluation protocol using 100 randomly sampled MSC instances and two independent human annotators making Yes/No judgments. Existing benchmark splits, training settings and testing procedures are retained; the retrieval-parameter experiments were already in v1 Appendix C.

E4.justification: The new human evaluation tests agreement between the LLM judge and human judgments, adding a limited evaluator-validation analysis. Existing component ablations, granularity and offline-training analyses, retrieval sensitivity, convergence analysis and case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 introduces Cohen's kappa estimates for human–human and human–LLM agreement in Table 7. Table 1 retains its three-run averaging statement; no increased run count, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports kappa values of 0.82 between humans and 0.71 and 0.69 between the LLM and each human. Existing benchmark and analysis results are unchanged, including v1 Figure 7 and Table 5, relocated as v2 Tables 5 and 6.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and mathematical expressions in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. The topic clarification is conceptual, and the added kappa evaluation introduces no formal definition, derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same two-component contribution and claims about retrieval and personalized-response improvements. The human evaluation adds supporting evidence without changing these core claims.

C2.justification: New Table 7 explicitly interprets the human–human and human–LLM agreement as 'Substantial agreement,' adding a limited assessment of evaluator consistency. Existing mechanism explanations, result interpretations and stated limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 8.8 documents the human annotation workflow: inputs shown, reuse of the existing judge instructions, and annotators' NLP expertise and non-author status. Existing hyperparameters, software, hardware, prompts and codebase access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds historical context citing Walker and Weizenbaum and references Mem0, MemGPT, Zep, Agent Workflow Memory and A-Mem. This modestly broadens related work without substantially changing RMM's positioning. Publication updates to existing citations are not new research coverage.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies 'topic,' makes small wording edits, and moves v1 Appendices C and D into Sections 8.7 and 8.8. Case studies and prompts are consequently renumbered, while most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 4–5 gain hatch patterns. v1 Figure 7 becomes main-text Table 5, and appendix Table 5 becomes Table 6 with an expanded caption. v2 adds agreement Table 7 and repositions Figure 6; the remaining displays are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: Section 8.8 and Table 7 add human agreement evidence for the MSC LLM judge, addressing a validation gap in v1. The topic clarification, patterned charts and more prominent placement of existing analyses also improve readability. These gains are limited: the human check covers 100 MSC instances, while the method, benchmark coverage and existing performance findings remain unchanged.
